title: The House That Was a Tree

chapters.title: This was a tree
narration: This was a tree. Now it's a house. And it cost less than a used car: $12,036.

chapters.title: The cheapest part
narration: Stay to the end, because the strangest number in it is the trees. They were the cheapest part.

chapters.title: The papercuts
narration: A new house sells for $665,299. $178,746 of that is fees and margins. Not one board. Not one hour on the house.

chapters.title: The biggest cut
narration: Borrow $100,000 and you pay back $227,544. The interest alone would build more than 10 of these.

chapters.title: Fifteen hands
narration: Every stud in that house went through 15 sets of hands. Every one of them took a cut.

chapters.title: So I cut them out
narration: So I cut them out. One chainsaw. One log. Eight wedges, and nobody measures an angle.

chapters.title: Two lengths
narration: 120 members in two lengths. One jig. Forty flat panels, built on the grass and lifted into a dome.

chapters.title: Even the floor
narration: Even the floor is free geometry. Cut a twenty foot log at 148.3 inches and what's left is 91.7: the golden ratio. Five logs make a pentagon.

chapters.title: The whole bill
narration: The whole bill is 9 lines, from one seller. $12,036, with the margin printed on it.

chapters.title: The trees
narration: And the trees? The frame and every wall closed in wood: 4 to 7 pines.

chapters.title: Not yet
narration: Is it engineered yet? No. That's the first thing the money buys. Everything else is open: every number you just heard is computed in code anyone can check.

chapters.title: Who it's for
narration: It isn't for everyone. It's for the eighteen-year-old, the veteran, the mother who's done paying for someone else's papercuts. Follow the build.
